sections.whatsHappening: You cannot bring a claim for these damages unless you give written notice of the claim to the clerk of the municipality. This notice must include the date, time, and location of the occurrence.
sections.whatToDoNext: You must serve the written notice upon or send it by registered mail to the clerk of the municipality.
sections.yourDeadline:
Give written notice of the claim to the clerk of the municipality. You have 10 days, counted from the occurrence of the injury.

This deadline is set by a statute rather than by the court's rules, and that changes how the days are counted. Under the rules a deadline landing on a Saturday moves to the next working day. Under the statute it does not — only Sunday and holidays are excluded. Do not assume a weekend gives you extra time.
sections.whatHappensAfter: If you do not give notice, you may not be able to bring a claim for damages. However, failure to give notice is not a bar to the action if the injured person has died as a result of the injury, or if a judge finds there is a reasonable excuse for the lack of notice and the municipality is not prejudiced in its defence.
